# Interndex pipeline

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-agent-playbook.mjs from lib/agent/playbook/phases.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Interndex holds the playbook, David's standards, his saved rules and his story library. Always start by calling `get_playbook` with the phase below: its standards and saved rules override anything here.

## Run: job description to built resume

Phase: `run`. David pastes a job description, or asks to run on a posting.

1. Work through every step without stopping for approval. Ask David nothing mid-run unless a step below says to.
2. If the posting is already in Interndex, call get_application_brief and get_run_state for it and continue from the first step not marked done. Never redo a done step unless David asks (then pass force: true). Never call get_job during a run; the brief has what you need.
3. Read the posting once and extract: company, exact posting title, location, the employer's job id, the posting link, partner functions the role works with, and the requirements in the posting's words. Mark must_have every required qualification and every main responsibility, the duties the role exists to do; mark nice_to_have only what the posting calls preferred, a plus or a bonus. Give a degree requirement its own requirement, with the level and every field it names. Call create_application_from_jd once with all of it. If it reports an existing application, use that id.
4. Fit read. Open it with the profile's year of study and academic standing as plain info, one short line each (for example: Year of study: 3rd year. Academic standing: 2nd year.). They are facts, not warnings. Then check only the posting's own stated eligibility (graduation window, degree level, year of study or standing) against the profile in this playbook; a year requirement is met if either value meets it. If they rule David out, stop and say why in one line. When the posting asks for a degree in fields his degree and program do not cover (a B.S. in Computer Science for a BCom in Business Technology Management), say so as a degree risk in the fit read and count it as a gap; complete_run checks this. Otherwise decide: each requirement matched to a story, true gaps (by requirement number), words to mirror, and the verdict by this rule, counting the must_have requirements that are true gaps: none is Strong fit, up to half is Moderate fit, more than half is Long shot. complete_run checks the verdict against gap_requirements and refuses one that is too strong. Then choose the template (zero2sudo for PM, TPM, data, AI and solutions roles; jakes for consulting and business roles).
5. Never mention work authorization, school semesters or terms, IBM, or other applications anywhere in the run.
6. Tailor with the Positioning playbook in the standards below. Call search_stories once with the requirements, the angles the role calls for, and the template.
7. The library is a source of facts, not fixed text. For each bullet, either reuse a variant as is, or write a new bullet from the story's facts (its summary, variants and explain notes), mirroring the posting's language and following the house style and the stretch rules in the standards. Every claim must trace to the story's facts. Employers, titles and dates always come from the library unchanged. Frame leadership and club roles toward the posting's scope (stakeholder coordination, process improvement, operations, budgeting, communication) using only the story's facts, never as plain event logistics. Bold only the phrases and numbers that mirror the posting's words or prove a requirement it lists, never every number; complete_run checks this. At most 2 drafts per new bullet, and give every new number an explain note David could say in two sentences.
8. Every bullet runs exactly two lines, the last at least 80% full. Only entries marked one_line_ok in this playbook may have one-line bullets, at least 80% full. Call check_bullets on the whole page with the template, passing those bullets' indexes as one_line_ok. Fix every failure and check again, line_fill included: once the template is calibrated its character targets come from David's real page, and fixing them now is what lets the run use one build. Never show David a page that has failures.
9. If the template shows calibrated false in this playbook, call calibrate_template for it once. If no base resume is saved for it yet, ask David for the resume.lol id of its base resume.
10. Write the resume content with the entry keys listed under the template in this playbook. Give bullets for every entry marked needs_bullets, or set omit: true. Set section_order only to move a section (projects can go above experience). The entries are the library's experiences: employers, titles, dates, locations and schools come from the library and are never changed, and the base resume supplies only the layout, section order and header. Give each entry the number of bullets its playbook entry shows (bullets min to max), which is David's layout; complete_run refuses other counts. search_stories includes a story for every experience, and one-line bullets are fine under entries marked one_line_ok. Leave an entry off only with omit: true. Leave the interests line off (include_interests false) unless the company's culture clearly invites it; the build adds it from David's profile when the page has room. Set mirrored_title only when David asks.
11. Save and build with one complete_run call: the fit read, the resume content, new variants with their explain notes, and any cover letter or answers. Do not wait for approval before building. If it reports failures, nothing was saved: fix them and call it again.
12. Read the build result. The build fills the page itself: page_adjustments lists bullets it added from the library (show each with its explain note in the summary) or cut. A run uses exactly one build: never call rebuild_with_edits during the run, because the second build is David's, for his edits at the apply step. layout_check passed: done. failed: for each bullet it names, give an exact rewording in the summary, ready to pass to rebuild_with_edits: same facts from the story, house style as in the gold set, long enough to fill its last line at least 80%. Never ask David to write them. skipped: the server could not print the PDF; say so in one line, give David the resume.lol link to print from, and list any layout_failures the same way. If the build call itself failed before building (resume.lol unreachable), call build_resume with the tailored_resume_id; a failed call does not use a build.
13. Finish with one short summary: the fit read, the PDF link, the posting link, and new explain notes next to the bullets that use them. If the posting asks for a cover letter or questions, draft them from the library and search_answers and include them. End with one usage line from complete_run's usage: tool calls and estimated tokens of tool traffic, noting that the chat's own tokens are not included. No explanations unless David asks.
14. If David changes anything while applying, use rebuild_with_edits with his exact edits (it saves each one as an example). If an edit breaks a rule, tell him in one line and pass keep_failing_edits: true only if he keeps it. At most 2 builds per resume in total. Save any general instruction he gives with add_rule.

## Library session: write and polish story variants

Phase: `library_session`. David asks to work on the story library, add a new story, or fill angle gaps.

1. Load the library with search_stories for the angles or requirements David names.
2. Convert story_voice variants to house style, add new stories David describes, and write consulting, PM and data versions of stories that lack them.
3. Run check_bullets on every new variant and fix every failure before saving.
4. Give every variant an explain note: one line David could say in an interview, drafted from the story's context.
5. Save each variant with save_variant (source library_session). Show David one compact list at the end, not one message per variant.

## Import: seed the library from David's resumes

Phase: `import`. David shares his recent resumes to set up the story library. Run once; running again changes nothing.

1. Read every resume David shares. Group the bullets into stories (about 25 in total): one story per piece of work, with all its wordings as variants. Write each story's summary as its fact sheet: every fact, number and tool behind the story, since runs write new bullets from these facts.
2. For each experience record the organization, official title, start and end month, location exactly as the most recent resume states them, and its resume section (experience, projects or leadership). Resumes are built from these, so they must be right.
3. Tag each variant house or story_voice using the standards below. Mark the gold set bullets in the standards is_gold.
4. Draft a one-line explain note for every variant that has a number. Show the notes as one compact list per experience; David approves all or fixes lines.
5. Ask David once for the fit-read profile if this playbook shows none: graduation month and year, degree and program, year of study, academic standing if it differs from year of study, the first month of the degree, and the school's location as resumes show it.
6. Call import_library with the experiences, stories, variants and profile. It is safe to call again: anything already saved is skipped. Save every general instruction David gave during the import with add_rule.
